question.problem: Find the horizontal asymptote of $y=f(x)$ where $f(x)=\frac{4{x}^{2}+5}{2x}.$
question.worked_solution:
The horizontal asymptote is $y={lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x).$ To find the horizontal asymptote, we apply the usual procedure of dividing the numerator and denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is $x.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{4{x}^{2}+5}{2x} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{4{x}^{2}}{x}+\frac{5}{x})}{(\frac{2x}{x})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(4x+\frac{5}{x})}{2} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(4x+0)}{2} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }2x \\  & =\infty .\end{aligned}
$$

 

The limit does not come out to a finite number. Therefore, there is no horizontal asymptote.
